task: torpedo, step 1: facts around the TORPEDO reading, checked 2026-10-07

order_on_page_1: Opening self-identification line (the usual 'This is the Zodiac speaking').
Immediately after it, a question whether the recipients have cracked the last cipher he sent (Z340, mailed 1969-11-08). Quote: "By the way have you cracked the last cipher I sent you?"
Next line: "My name is" followed by a long dash; the 13 symbols stand alone on the following line.

Then: he is curious how much reward money is on his head; he hopes they do not think he killed the 'blue meannie' (a police officer) with a bomb at the cop station (the 1970-02-16 Park Station bombing), although he had talked about killing school children with a bomb; he would not move in on someone else's territory; more glory in killing a cop than a kid because a cop can shoot back; he claims ten killed to date; there would have been more except his bus bomb was a dud, swamped out by rain.
letter_1970_04_20.page_2: Headed "The new bomb is set up like this"; a diagram of a bus on a road, the sun, photoelectric switches A and B, a car battery ('Car Bat'), a timer and a 'String of Bombs'; the text explains that breaking the sunbeam closes A and B is a cloudy-day disconnect so the bomb will not go off by accident. PS: he hopes they have fun working out whom he killed. Score line: crosshair sign = 10, SFPD = 0.
bomb_words_actually_in_the_letter: BOMB (2x in the page-1 text, 2x in the page-2 text)
BOMBS (diagram label 'String of Bombs', scan only)
letter_1970_04_20.torpedo_in_letter: No. The word torpedo does not occur in this letter (checked against both scans and the Wikisource transcription).
letter_1970_04_20.note: The cipher is the only text between the 'last cipher' question and the reward/bomb paragraph; the first bomb mention is on the sixth handwritten line below the cipher, in the same paragraph.

garlick.who: Ryan Garlick, computer science and engineering faculty, University of North Texas; earlier led a 2007 distributed Z340 search and appeared with Bauer, Knight and Oranchak on the History Channel team (arXiv:2403.17350 sections 2.1 and 2.4, local copy data/sources/arxiv_2403.17350.html).
garlick.claim_2020: Forum post dated 2020-12-22 on forum.zodiackillerciphers.com ('Ryan Garlick's Z13 solution') links a PDF at cse.unt.edu/~garlick/research/papers/Zodiac-my-name-is-Z13-solution-question-mark.pdf. Reading: Z340 key on the six shared symbols, circled glyph = T, hooked T = P, giving the letters DREATATOTPEDO read as 'Dr. eat a totpedo (torpedo)', aimed at Dr. Marsh's challenge. Forum members noted the PDF link was dead by 2020-12-23 and objected that mixing old-key symbols with new symbols is odd.
garlick.pdf_archive_check: Wayback CDX listing of cse.unt.edu/~garlick/research/papers/* (queried 2026-10-07) has Zodiac-340.pdf and older papers but no capture of the Z13 PDF; we could not read it.
garlick.claim_2025: David Oranchak's YouTube episode 'Let's Crack Zodiac #23 - Dr Garlick's solution', published 2025-04-08 (page metadata: uploadDate 2025-04-08, length 1985 s, about 33 min). The description says Garlick reveals his Z13 solution there for the first time, which is inconsistent with the December 2020 forum post. Wikipedia (Zodiac Killer, 'Proposed solutions') summarises it as 'Dr. Eat a Torpedo', an insult directed at D. C. B. Marsh. We could not retrieve the video transcript (captions endpoint returned nothing), so the in-video reasoning for circle = T and hook = P is not verified here.
garlick.letters_vs_reading: Under one circle symbol his assignment yields DREATATOTPEDO: the third circle gives T, so the published reading needs the misspelling TOTPEDO. TORPEDO itself needs the circle at position 8 to be R while the circles at 4 and 6 are T, i.e. at least two different circle symbols (z13.circles_distinct), which no transcription asserts.

marsh.who: Donald C. B. Marsh: Ph.D. in mathematics, University of Colorado (Boulder), 1954, dissertation on indefinite ternary quadratic forms (Mathematics Genealogy Project id 12266). Mathematics professor at the Colorado School of Mines; long-time member and then president of the American Cryptogram Association; the SFPD asked him for help with the ciphers; he independently verified the Hardens' Z408 solution (arXiv:2403.17350 section 2, citing a 1969-11-14 newspaper article).
marsh.dare: San Francisco Examiner, 1969-10-22, page 9: 'Cipher Expert Dares Zodiac To "Tell" Name'. Marsh said the killer would not dare reveal his name in a cipher to established experts and invited him to send the ACA a cipher that truly includes his name (zodiacrevisited.com 'name cipher motivation'; Pelling, Cipher Mysteries 2017-12-16).
marsh.later: In a 1970-01-06 Vallejo newspaper interview Marsh said the ACA had not spent much effort on Z340 and expected its content to be as valueless as the first cipher's (arXiv:2403.17350 section 1.5).
marsh.timing: Z340 was mailed 1969-11-08, 17 days after the dare; Pelling (2017) argues Z340, not Z13, was the reply. Z13 came about six months after the dare, introduced by 'My name is', which matches the dare's wording; Garlick and others read Z13 as the reply.
marsh.dr_fits: Yes as a title: Marsh held a doctorate and the press called him Dr. Marsh and Professor Marsh. Whether 'DR' at the start of Z13 refers to him is the hypothesis itself; 'DR' is also simply the first two letters the Z340 key gives for the symbols A and E.
